These factors are mapped through a mental event L, representing an intermediate cognitive process between stimulus S and response R. The structure implies a hierarchical decomposition of behavior into genetic and environmental determinants, with L acting as a mediator. The absence of generalized S→R diagrams suggests a focus on singular causality rather than probabilistic transitions. This framework supports a dual-process theory where H/T define baseline capacity, while L governs dynamic integration. The failure mode arises when H or T are insufficiently defined, leading to undefined factor contributions and thus unpredictable behavior.
